filesChanged: Two forward merges of main (#2145, #2153, #2126; then #2162), seventeen conflicted files resolved so both sides survive, and this branch's migration renumbered 0018 because main landed an 0017.
packages/envoy/internal/broker/oauth/introspect.go: Introspect reads the kind the library reports finding and answers anything that is not a live access token as not live.

packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/agentsecrets/client.go, internal/dispatch/api/credential_requests.go: an unreadable ServiceAccount token file is its own error type, answered 500 AGENT_SECRETS_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_UNREADABLE and logged once with its path, instead of being reported as the broker being unreachable.

packages/envoy/scripts/dev-broker.sh and its test, packages/envoy/cmd/agent-secrets-devrelay/, packages/dispatch/e2e/{run-server.sh,harness-broker.ts,local-instance.ts,fake-broker.ts,fake-broker-account-token}, docs/site/media/broker/{rig.sh,README.md}: each local path gets a caller identity of its own.
packages/envoy/cmd/broker/main.go: the two issuer-key reads run on the serving context, as #2162 requires of every boot call after the bind, so a signal during them drains rather than kills.

docs/site/src/content/docs/broker/{operate.md,concepts.md,guides/*}, packages/dispatch/{AGENTS.md,README.md}, packages/envoy/{AGENTS.md,CHANGELOG.md} and four Go comments: no instruction to set a removed bearer.
trickyParts: The tester's red test in packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_test.go could not be kept out of the diff: the file's own helper and nine refusal rows set the component input the task removes, so the file stopped compiling. The red test function itself is unchanged, verified byte for byte against the tester's commit; everything else in that file moved to the new input.

dev-oidc-issuer's first test was flaky: it minted a two-second token and verified it again while waiting for the rewrite, so a loaded machine failed on 'token expired'. The lifetime is six seconds now and only the rewritten token is verified, which still proves the rewrite happens before the token lapses. It was caught by -count=5 and under a parallel run, not by the first green run.

main's #2162 moved the one boot call that runs after the bind onto the serving context, so a pod the load balancer may already be reaching drains rather than dies. This branch's two issuer-key reads also run after the bind and were on the signal context; they are on serving now, and the comment that called the other one 'the one boot call that runs after the bind' says what is true.
deviations: None from the architect's rulings this round. The scope question the tester raised -- how the local run gets a caller identity -- was answered by the architect (a local OIDC issuer and a listed dev account, reusing the rig's issuer) and is built that way.

The architect also asked that the minted access token's lifetime be short by default; it already is, BROKER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECONDS defaults to 900 (fifteen minutes), and the corrected comment and pull request bullet now name it as what bounds a deleted pod's reach.
openQuestions: Real liveness checking at exchange time is not in this slice: the architect ruled it a child issue of its own if it is wanted. The claim now says what the offline check proves.
main has moved twice during this round and may move again; a third conflict is a third forward merge, not a reshaping of the slice.
discoveredComplexity: main@origin's own cmd/broker tests did not compile at 3ca092a69891: service_accounts_test.go and service_account_scope_test.go still called the startBroker form #2162 replaced. They are fixed in the merge rather than left, since the branch cannot be green while its base is not.

This pod has no psql, which dev-broker.sh has always needed, so the local walk-through was run with a pgx stand-in for its three psql calls, outside the repository; the script itself ran unchanged. The same pod cannot run a workload in the cluster (kubectl auth can-i create services answers no), so the Postgres every live run needs is a standalone build fetched onto the issue's volume.
